chunks: And from it, regarding the attribute of the learned one:
The learned one is he who knows his worth, and sufficient for a man is ignorance that he does not know his worth.
And indeed, among the most hated of men to Allah is a servant whom Allah has left to himself, deviating from the straight path, moving without a guide.
If he is called to the cultivation of this world, he works, but if he is called to the cultivation of the Hereafter, he is sluggish.
As though what he works for is obligatory upon him, and as though what he delays is excused from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a true scholar (al-'Alim) in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this definition of the 'Alim' (scholar) emphasizes that true knowledge is rooted in *ma'rifah* (gnosis) of one's spiritual station and limitations, rather than mere accumulation of facts. Sharif al-Radi highlights the tragic irony of the ignorant scholar who, despite being entrusted with his own soul, neglects the Hereafter while busying himself with worldly affairs, treating obligatory duties as optional and optional acts as burdensome.
